Subject: API credential options + short PoC scope / action list

Hi Samantha / LedgerCo team —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the PoC:

1) Credentialing options we discussed (pros/cons):
   - API keys (short-term): simplest for initial PoC, quick to provision, lower setup friction but requires strict rotation and per-env separation.
   - OAuth 2.0 (authorization code / client credentials): recommended if you want user-scoped access and long-term SSO compatibility.
   - JWT service accounts (short-lived): best for server-to-server calls with centralized rotation via your KMS/HSM.

2) Redwood-specific items to validate during PoC:
   - SDK bootstrap using ephemeral tokens (we can pre-seed a short-lived API key for testing).
   - Routing policy for dev vs prod endpoints (we’ll show route-by-model config).
   - Embeddings & reranking access scope (separate key or RBAC?).
   - Structured output / tool-calling: confirm which external tools will be invoked and any credentials needed for those tool calls.

3) Acceptance criteria (simple PoC):
   - Demo an end-to-end call that: authenticates -> runs a structured tool call -> returns embeddings for a sample query -> shows KV cache behavior.
   - Latency under 450ms (p95) for our sample prompt set.
   - Confirmed key rotation procedure in your sandbox account.

Attachments: credentialing-matrix.xlsx (matrix of options) and PoC checklist (short).

Proposed next steps / owners:
   - Rishi: schedule SDK onramp session and share test keys.
   - Marissa: prepare PoC checklist and sample prompts.
   - Samantha: confirm procurement timeline and who owns service account rotation on your side.

Can you confirm the person who will handle service-account rotation on LedgerCo and whether you prefer to start with API keys or go straight to JWTs for the PoC?

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks, Rishi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We prefer starting with JWT service accounts for the PoC. Security team wants to validate rotation flow with our internal KMS rather than testing with static API keys.
- Procurement note: we'll need an estimated cost snapshot for the PoC (1-2 weeks, dev capacity) to sign the temporary PO. I’ve looped procurement.
- Rotation owner: that will be me for the PoC (we’ll use a dedicated service account in our sandbox).

On the tooling side, we have a reranker microservice that will call Redwood embeddings. That service is currently authenticated via an internal service account; we will need the SDK to support token refresh for short-lived JWTs (or accept a signed JWT assertion flow).

Samantha

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Samantha. A couple quick notes on the implementation path we propose for JWT/service-account flow:

- SDK: we'll provide a minimal helper that exchanges a signed JWT for a short-lived Redwood access token. That helper will be packaged in our Node and Python SDKs.
- Rotation: recommended cadence for the PoC is daily ephemeral tokens backed by your KMS; production we typically advise automatic rotation via KMS-backed secrets and a 1-3 hour TTL for tokens used by runtime services.
- RBAC: we’ll scope embeddings/reranker privileges to a dedicated role so your reranker microservice gets only embedding/transform rights — no model administrative privileges.

Ben — could you prepare the sample Node snippet that shows the signed-jwt exchange + simple embeddings call? I can drop that into the PoC checklist.

Marissa

Attaching a short code example in the Drive link. Inline snippet for quick reference: 

// Node example (very small):
// 1) create and sign JWT locally using your service account private key
// 2) call /v1/auth/token-exchange with the signed assertion
// 3) use returned access_token for subsequent SDK calls (embeddings/tool-calls)

const axios = require('axios');
async function exchangeJwt(signedJwt) {
  const r = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/auth/token-exchange', {assertion: signedJwt});
  return r.data.access_token;
}

Notes: token TTL for PoC is configurable; we’ll set to 4h for initial tests. Also: for structured tool-calls that invoke your downstream services, include a mapping table of external tool credentials in the PoC checklist so we can validate tool permissions during the demo.
